workflow.note: Kokoro narrator + Qwen3-TTS Base clone for dialogue. Voice direction comes from data/voice-profiles.json; selected refs were chosen before the location-specific language profiles were formalized and require human reevaluation against them. ICL clone knobs (temp/top_p/x_vector_only) live in docs/wip/qwen-icl-clone-defaults.json — do not use x_vector_only. Per-line [QwenInstruct] adds performance colour only. Selected refs: static/assets/voices/en/.

refText: Ship systems are stable. Propellant, guidance, and communications check out. We hold the planned acceleration and stay on the contact schedule. I will say this once, clearly, so the record is clean.

Zao.instruct: Female, mid-40s, dry functional contralto with slight rasp from years near machinery, chest resonance, almost no vibrato. Mandarin prosody carried into formal scientific Singapore English: marked consonants, even rhythm, falling phrase endings, few contractions, no colloquial particles. Calm, precise technical authority; not warm or theatrical.

Voss.instruct: Male, early 50s, full baritone with deep chest resonance, steady breath, almost no rasp. Germanic or Nordic prosody carried into standard institutional Toronto English: hard consonants, very clear vowels, even pauses, few fillers. Formal Canadian command presence; authority without shouting.

Harlan.instruct: Male, early 40s, lighter baritone than a captain, forward metallic edge, jaw tension audible in consonants. Polished southern British English formed through naval service in Portsmouth: precise, strategically courteous, unnervingly even, with understated threat. Surface warmth with something cold underneath; controlled, not booming.

Elin.instruct: Female, early 30s, light mezzo with audible breath at rest, thinner resonance. South Indian prosody carried into urban technology English learned in Bengaluru: softer consonants, syllable timing, slight rises when unsure; flatter and faster during technical analysis. Intelligent, careful, not childish.

Sorell.instruct: Female, early 30s, warm expressive mezzo with wide pitch range, forward mask resonance made for classrooms. French prosody carried into Canadian English learned in Montréal's francophone environment: softened R, flexible musical intonation, natural contractions, very precise diction. Passionate when defending an idea, but this sample should stay composed and clear.

Okoye.instruct: Female, firm contralto with marked chest resonance and direct consonant attack. Educated Nigerian English learned in Enugu with Igbo prosody: syllable-timed rhythm, very clear consonants, firm falling intonation at phrase ends. Security-officer delivery trained for commands under risk; calm authority, unambiguous, not soft, no caricature.

Reporter.instruct: Female, mid-30s, clear mid-register mezzo with studio presence and chest support, almost no rasp. General American English shaped by international news broadcasting (Washington, D.C.): steady contemporary news cadence, carefully articulated proper names, emphasis reserved for verifiable contrasts, accessible international diction, no regional caricature and no theatrical drama. Speak clearly at a noticeably slower, deliberate, unhurried pace. Authority without shouting.
